Vampire.name: Vampire
Vampire.summary: The archetypal undead creature of European folklore, immortalized as an aristocratic predator who preys on the living under cover of darkness
Vampire.physicalDescription: Pale skin, fanged teeth, red eyes, aristocratic appearance, casts no reflection
Vampire.powers: Shapeshifting (bat, wolf, mist), Hypnosis, Superhuman strength, Immortality
Vampire.origin: Bitten by another vampire, Dying in sin, Improper burial, Suicide
Vampire.weaknesses: Sunlight, Garlic, Holy water, Crosses, Silver, Wooden stake through heart, Running water
Vampire.feedingMethod: Biting the neck, draining blood of living victims at night
Vampire.culturalContext: Rooted in Eastern European fear of the undead and disease outbreaks; popularized in Western culture by Bram Stoker's Dracula (1897)
Vampire.sources: Bram Stoker's Dracula, Vampyre by John Polidori (1819)

Strigoi.name: Strigoi
Strigoi.summary: A malevolent undead spirit from Romanian folklore, one of the primary inspirations for the modern vampire myth, feared for draining the life force of family members and livestock
Strigoi.year: Ancient Romanian folklore, documented formally in the 1700s
Strigoi.physicalDescription: Ruddy complexion, two hearts, red hair, blue eyes, may appear as they did in life
Strigoi.powers: Shapeshifting (cat, dog, flea), invisibility, draining life force, causing disease in livestock
Strigoi.origin: Dying unbaptized, born with a caul, living a sinful life, being cursed by a witch
Strigoi.weaknesses: Garlic, iron, hawthorn, burning the corpse, placing millet in the grave to distract counting
Strigoi.feedingMethod: Draining life force and blood from family members and livestock while they sleep
Strigoi.culturalContext: Deeply embedded in Romanian peasant culture, the Strigoi was feared as a returning family member. Corpses were often exhumed and staked to prevent their return
Strigoi.sources: Romanian Vampires by Agnes Murgoci (1926), The Vampire in Romanian Belief and Folklore by Tudor Pamfile
